root.summary: Before we write a line of Go: get the Python engine into a state where the port is a transcription, not a redesign. The forcing function is one line — the same plugin file, unmodified, renders byte-identical HTML under both engines. Everything below is conscripted by it. (v2 — corrected after Mr. Dragon's catch: there is no heavy-two exception, and raw() is a security debt to eliminate, not a feature to bless.)

facets.The endpoint: One plugin file → byte-identical HTML on Python AND Go.
facets.The method: Write top-down by dependency. The top line demands every layer beneath it; the build order is that chain reversed.
facets.We stand here: A working Python reference engine, 24 primitives (22 already clean), ~156 green tests, golden HTML on disk.
facets.The crux (your call): Where does expressiveness come from — composing safe atoms, or a raw() escape hatch? (Answer: composition. raw() dies.)

blocks.text: The same plugin file, unmodified, renders byte-identical HTML under both the Python reference and the Go binary.
blocks.sub: That single line is the forcing function. We don't argue for the prerequisites — this line conscripts them, visibly, and you watch the demand cascade.

sections.name: Why this is the line
sections.summary: The reframe you handed me, stated as the endpoint.

items.name: The binary is the full engine
items.desc: No reduced-scope port. The public artifact does everything the Python reference does — render, freeze, lint, roll, serve. Scope is settled; it is not a crux.

items.name: A plugin must not be host-language code
items.desc: If a primitive is Python, porting means hand-rewriting 24 files into Go and re-blessing goldens twice. If a primitive is engine-language-independent, you port the CORE once and the library is shared, untouched.

sections.name: The hard properties (each names a prerequisite)
sections.summary: Read the endpoint's properties — each one secretly conscripts a layer below.

items.name: “the same plugin file, unmodified”
items.desc: → plugins cannot be host-language code → a language-independent plugin format. (Layer −1.)

items.name: “byte-identical”
items.desc: → both engines must agree on escape table, JSON key ordering, number and newline rules → a frozen wire spec. (Layer −2.)

items.name: “under both engines”
items.desc: → a conformance oracle that runs the SAME inputs on both and diffs bytes → language-neutral golden pairs. (Layer −3.)

items.name: “renders”
items.desc: → a stable contract for what a plugin is → the 7-member primitive trait, already declared language-agnostic in core/primitive.py. (Layer −4 — reuse.)

sections.name: The gotcha layer (named out loud)
sections.summary: Every real design has one unglamorous landmine. Here it is.

items.name: Silent cross-language divergence in the wire spec
items.desc: html.escape turns ' into ' and " into "; Python preserves dict insertion order; floats and trailing newlines format a specific way. A Go port that guesses any of these produces HTML that looks right and diffs wrong. The wire spec is the antidote — and it is boring, which is why it gets skipped. We will not skip it.

nodes.title: What a plugin is — and the raw() trap

blocks.text: Expressiveness comes from composing safe atoms — not from a raw() hole punched through the page.
blocks.sub: Your catch: statemachine isn't a primitive monster. It's a set of simple primitive shapes PLUS a template for composing them. That dissolves the 'heavy two' and exposes the real decision.

left.title: The raw() trap (what I almost blessed)
items: “Some primitives are too hard — let them inject raw HTML.”
A stranger's source.json can inject <script> → runs in the reader's browser.
Freeze gate catches external refs, NOT inline injection.
It's a confession the primitive vocabulary ran out.
Betrays covenant II (expression is the payload) and the §6 security mission.

right.title: Composition (the right answer)
items: Primitives are safe atoms: structured in, escaped out, no raw.
A composition is primitives nested in data — a template.
statemachine becomes: general primitives + a composition, raw()=0.
A stranger can only COMPOSE safe atoms — no injection truck-route.
Expression scales by growing the shared vocabulary, not by punting.

rows.label: Expressive enough for the 2 bespoke pages
Safe when a STRANGER writes source.json

options.text: Structured primitives composed into templates — no raw(), no expression mini-language ✓ LOCKED
Keep a raw() HTML passthrough as an escape hatch
WASM / compiled code plugins — both engines host a runtime

blocks.title: Decided — a composition is just data (no new machinery)

options.text: A composition IS a source.json that nests primitive blocks (templates are data, like everything else) ✓ LOCKED
Add a named, reusable 'template/component' concept to the engine

sections.name: The measurement (your catch, quantified)
sections.summary: I used file-LOC as a proxy for complexity. It lied. Here is the truth.

items.name: raw() is concentrated in exactly 2 files
items.desc: statemachine (26 sites) + citizenlifecycle (14 sites) = 40 of 42. The other 22 primitives use raw() zero times — they are already clean, safe, structured plugins.

citations.note: 13 trivial template primitives in one file — NOT one hard primitive

items.name: There is no 'heavy two'
items.desc: statemachine is 13 tiny primitives (Kicker, Nav, Rails, Swim, Duo, TransitionTable…), each as simple as hero. Nothing computes geometry — CSS does layout; the data carries col/style/cls verbatim. The 250/137 LOC was bundling, not difficulty.

citations.note: same shape: loop + conditional + esc + interpolation

sections.name: Why raw() must die
sections.summary: Two reasons, and they are the same reason.

items.name: Security — the stranger's source.json
items.desc: We ship a signed binary to people who write their OWN source.json. A raw() pathway lets a malicious source inject markup/script the reader's browser executes. The freeze gate stops exfil (external refs), not inline injection. Designing raw() out removes the seam entirely — the §6 'field of fear' answer made literal.

items.name: Expressiveness — a raw() is a missing primitive
items.desc: Every raw() call is a place the vocabulary ran out and we punted to hand-HTML. The 40 sites are a punch-list: each becomes a structured primitive or a composition. raw()→0 is both the security gate AND the expressiveness win.

sections.name: The residual judgment (a P3 detail, not a top crux)
sections.summary: One real design call, smaller than the two above.

items.name: Primitive-extraction granularity
items.desc: When we dissolve statemachine, what's the right grain? Is 'swim-lane grid' one primitive or several (lane / beat / cell)? Judgment call, made during P4, provable by the golden oracle either way.

sections.name: P1 — Extract golden pairs
sections.summary: Unglamorous, and the one thing everything downstream needs. Nothing has an oracle without it.

items.name: Lift fixtures into data
items.desc: fixtures.py builds doc-trees as Python dicts; the self-doc and examples already have source.json. Convert every golden case to a checked-in input.json.

citations.note: golden inputs live as Python dicts today

items.name: Replace substring asserts with byte-diff
items.desc: Tests like assertIn("class='badges'", html) can't run cross-language. Diff full output against expected/*.html.

items.name: A neutral harness
items.desc: A runner that takes a case dir, renders input.json, diffs bytes against expected/. Both engines call the same harness contract.

sections.name: P2 — Write the wire spec
sections.summary: The contract Go matches instead of guessing. Short on purpose.

items.name: Escape table
items.desc: html.escape semantics: & < > and quote=True (' → ', " → "). With raw() removed, escape is the ONLY text path — which is exactly what makes the wire spec small.

items.name: Ordering & formatting
items.desc: dict/JSON key insertion order preserved; number formatting; trailing-newline policy on each rendered file.

items.name: Palette token resolution
items.desc: How var(--token) names resolve; which primitives are palette-free vs palette-bound (callout is loud if a key is undeclared).

sections.name: P3 — Design the plugin format
sections.summary: The crux, decided and proven small before scaling.

items.name: Spec the format
items.desc: Per Crux 1: iteration (with index/last metadata), conditional, map-lookup-with-default, escape — and COMPOSITION (a block may nest child blocks). No raw(), no expression language. The minimum that expresses decisionmatrix AND lets statemachine be a composition.

items.name: Prove on three
items.desc: Re-express hero (trivial), decisionmatrix (loop+map+default), descent (loop+conditional+connector). Green via P1 or the format is wrong.

sections.name: P4 — Dissolve the 2 compositions, kill raw()
sections.summary: The security-and-expressiveness phase. The 40 raw() sites are the punch-list.

items.name: Extract general shapes into primitives
items.desc: The reusable atoms hiding inside statemachine/citizenlifecycle (lane, beat, cell, track, snode, transition-row…) become real library primitives — structured, no raw().

citations.note: Swim etc. are general grid atoms, not page-specific

items.name: Re-express the 2 pages as compositions
items.desc: state-machine.html and citizen-lifecycle.html become source.json that nests those primitives — no bespoke .py renderer. Byte-identical via P1's golden.

items.name: The gate: raw() == 0
items.desc: Add a test that greps the primitive library for raw() and fails if any remain; then delete raw() from the ctx contract entirely. The injection seam is closed by construction.

citations.note: raw = passthrough — the line to remove once nothing needs it

sections.name: P5 — Convert the clean 22 to data
sections.summary: Mechanical once the format is proven; each gated by the oracle.

items.name: One primitive at a time, stay green
items.desc: Honor the strangler proof: every already-published page stays byte-identical as each primitive moves from code to data.

sections.name: P6 — Freeze & tag the reference
sections.summary: Settle the loose end, then declare the spec frozen.

items.name: Resolve widget #2 honestly
items.desc: Fix the stale-banner copy + contrast in lib/feedback.{js,css}; re-bless goldens ONCE. Under the new architecture this is a one-time reference edit — the language-neutral golden pairs carry forward to Go unchanged, so the old 'double re-bless' fear is gone.

items.name: Tag Python as spec-of-record
items.desc: The reference engine self-hosts the doc and is the oracle. Go ports the CORE against it, green at every line.
